body: **2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — wired dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature and its `accessibility_tree` override, made the shell build and refresh the tree through `Document::accessibility_tree`, and gave every Dioxus element node its stable id as `author_id` (no TextRun, document-root or Window node). This is where decision/accessibility-tree-through-document-method and contract/accessibility-tree/author-id come from. A layout read addressed by stable id resolves through the same `author_id`, so it has to take the id the tree carries and not invent a second id scheme.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — made the snapshot take role, name and focus from the accessibility tree, with no second role or name mapping, and added the snapshot to the `accessibility` feature's gated set. This is the precedent for every later reader: the new layout read reuses the snapshot's bounds (scope fct-tlegbc3w) and must add no role or name mapping of its own.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the actionable-key rule (anything an agent can act on reads an author key) and its `unkeyed_actionable` check. Trap: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or a role, because that moves the pinned Tab order. A minimal layout fixture (flex child, grid item, positioned or transformed box) that adds controls must key them and leave focus order alone.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — made a falsy `hidden` stop dropping a node, so an element rendered `hidden: false` is laid out and stays in the tree and the snapshot, while a truthy `hidden` still excludes it. This bears on the hidden-content rows: an element the layout read is asked about may be laid out yet excluded, or excluded by `display: none`.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — added `Snapshot::to_text` as one more reader of the snapshot model, put it behind the `accessibility` feature, and had the crate doc name each gated item. This is a precedent for how a new reader joins the gated set (decision/agent-readers-behind-accessibility) and for keeping the crate doc's list in step.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — made the tree refresh on a non-empty changed set and stated what marks that set: node creation, hover, active, scroll and layout do not. The diff became one more reader of the snapshot model, with the `accessibility` feature gating it. This is the origin of decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change and decision/changed-set-marks. A read-only layout read must mark nothing, and a layout-only move marks no changed set.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — at the time, the session library `escher-driver` named no dioxus-native-dom feature, and the decision was left to the first entry that reads the snapshot through a session. The founder also ratified the refresh on change and the changed-set contract (2026-10-07). This is the history behind decision/driver-requires-accessibility and decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — a harness settle neither reads nor drains the changed set, and a freshly booted document holds a non-empty set, so a check that reads the set as "what this step changed" must drain it first. This is the source of decision/harness-settle-leaves-changed-set (guard `stand_settle`). A check that the layout read "changes nothing" by reading `has_changes` after boot must drain first.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own: `role` and `name` are field names of its result nodes. This is the source of decision/driver-schema-has-no-role-set. If the layout answer is a driver verb, its schema adds closed words (layout modes, placement kinds) without a role or name vocabulary of its own.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — made `escher-driver` name `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom unconditionally, with no `[features]` table of its own, because its executor reads the snapshot. The feature reaches both seven_guis binaries, and still no platform adapter is built. This is the source of decision/driver-requires-accessibility. A layout verb in `execute.rs` can rely on the snapshot's bounds under that feature.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — an MCP tool result reads the snapshot model and nothing else, with no second role or name mapping. This is the precedent for the scope's `mcp/` listing and results if the layout read becomes a verb on every carrier.

**2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit** — the chunk that worked a scrolling box's bounds and hit. Its a11y amendment only recorded that a click on a plain button leaves nothing focused. It is a prior nearby change in the snapshot's bounds of scrolled boxes, which the layout read's "scroll that moves it from where layout put it" case extends.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — added `DiffNode::differs` (closed words) and the node keys' help (`help`) as readers of the snapshot model. The Flight Booker's Book names nodes that only moved as `[bounds]`. This is a precedent for describing a bounds-only move in closed words, and for the self-description (`describe.rs`) that the scope says a new verb must extend.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — made the driver's `screenshot` one more reader of the model's bounds: an element shot by stable id is its bounds rounded outward and cropped to what can be seen. A shot changes nothing (no focus move, `has_changes` false, empty next diff). This is the source of contract/driver-screenshot/element-shot and decision/screenshot-changes-nothing, the model for the layout read's "changes nothing" proof and its bounds reading.

**2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness** — built `Harness::text_contrast`, which reads an element's pair and font metrics from computed styles (backgrounds composited to the first opaque ancestor, `None` under opacity, filter or background image). This is a precedent reader of Stylo computed style per element, which the layout read's "inputs from the computed style" leg parallels.

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** (the enabled-state walks entry) — proved both halves of the refresh headlessly on the stand, and proved that the `&dyn Document` tree equals the document's, carrying stable ids only. It also re-homed the stand's platform adapter and AT witness to a residual. This bears on decision/a11y-tree-through-document-trait and on absence/assistive-technology-reach.

This is part of the hidden-content rows (contract/accessibility-tree/hidden-and-inert-nodes): an inert or hidden element the layout read is asked about has layout yet no snapshot node.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** — `text_contrast`'s first non-test caller is the in-process lint `Session::lint`, and its `contrast` reading adds no second formula. This is the lint whose findings name an element but not its cause, the observed gap behind v030-11 (scope fct-o7ne25b4).

A finding is written as `id` · `defect` · `bounds` · `ratio` · `required`: ids, closed words and numbers only. This is a precedent for a new read-only verb's carriage as a boundary widening, and for the closed-words-and-numbers field form that the scope's widening rule (fct-l235qet4) uses.

This is the origin of the select-option exception in decision/hidden-content-excluded and its twins. A layout read of an option that computes `display: none` has no Taffy box of its own, yet the snapshot holds it.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — added `Snapshot::text_parts` as a reader behind the `accessibility` feature, so the gated set grew to five. The driver's `snapshot` pages an over-budget screen (`SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`). Its pin reads none of those claims, so a change to the reach is made by hand. This is the source of decision/accessibility-reach-tier-0 and decision/capability-statement-reach-by-hand. **2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** (CSS properties as `CSSStyleDeclaration` accessors) — a script's `element.style` read or write of `display` or `visibility` goes through the inline style and reaches the tree's hidden-content exclusion. The inline style is one more input to the computed style that the layout read traces.

A `multiple` select's rows and groups read their own client rects, and its `value` reads its first chosen option in tree order. This is the source of contract/snapshot/multiple-select-rows-and-value, contract/snapshot/multiple-select-row-bounds and contract/snapshot/closed-select-option-bounds, which the layout read's "bounds the snapshot already reads" inherits.

A `multiple` select lays out its groups and rows as blocks. These are user-agent-sheet layout modes a "why it sits there" answer will meet on a select.

This is a precedent for telling a select's borrowed bounds from a real placement, and is part of the lint's link (scope fct-o7ne25b4).

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (a non-invertible transform takes no hit) — a transform whose determinant is 0 or not finite takes no hit for the whole subtree (`hit_non_invertible_transform`). This bears on the layout read's transformed-box case (scope fct-tlegbc3w, fct-bdtm4oct).

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the changed set where a list stands) — a single select's list opening or closing marks the set, and with a list open a page scroll or a move that closes it marks its select. A highlight or a wheel move inside the list marks nothing. This is the history of decision/changed-set-marks, which the read-only layout read must not disturb.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (what the snapshot and an assistive technology read of an open list) — an open list's row reads its painted row's bounds through `select_list_bounds` in the snapshot and the diff, and `differs` names `bounds`. No `expanded` node key exists, and the highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree. This is the source of contract/snapshot/open-list-row-bounds, contract/snapshot/select-list-rows and absence/snapshot-list-open-state. **2026-10-31-select-popup** (a long list and a sized `multiple` select) — a row brought into view writes the list's own `scroll_y` and moves no scroll chain or viewport. On a `multiple` select with a valid `size`, a key scrolls through `scroll_into_view`. This bears on the layout read's scroll-offset leg.

The list is an overlay placed outside author layout, which the answer's open placement kind may need to name.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the visual lint over an open list) — `Entry.in_select_box` reads an open row through `select_list_bounds`, and `clip_region` takes an open row's region from `visible_region` alone. This is a precedent for the lint's reading of placement and clipping, which the lint's link to the layout read touches.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (an open list has no motion) — motion on an open list is observed absent and needs no `advance` (`a_screen_read_after_a_step_reads_the_new_state_with_no_advance`). This is the source of absence/select-list-motion.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the capability statement's named limits) — the named limits in `docs/capabilities.md` under `## Accessibility reach` were edited by hand, and the pin still reads none of them. This is a precedent for decision/capability-statement-reach-by-hand when this chunk edits the capability statement.

Builds one read-only read of a named element's placement and size by its stable id: where it sits and at what size (the bounds the snapshot already reads) and why.
The why is the chain that placed it: its parent's layout mode, the inputs that mode took from the computed style, the containing block, and any scroll or transform that moves it.
It is read from the layout and computed style the engine already holds, with no second layout and no engine change; it runs no step and changes nothing, like snapshot, lint, graph and actions.
The answer's placement kind is an open set that reserves an app-placed-inside-canvas case naming an owner element by stable id; nothing in 0.3.0 produces it.
If the read is a driver verb it joins every ratified carrier, as lint, graph and actions did; its checks of a scrolled case are re-read when Taffy moves past #1372.

body: The new read's answer for a named element: its bounds as the snapshot already reads them, plus why — its parent's layout mode (block, flex, grid, inline, absolute or fixed positioning, a float), the inputs that mode took from computed style (sizing, margins, offsets, the parent's alignment and gaps), its containing block, and any scroll or transform moving it.
The element is named by its stable id, the same id the snapshot, graph and actions answers carry; an unknown or unplaced id is a refusal with a closed cause, as the driver's refusal causes are.

The answer's placement kind is not a closed set: it reserves a case placed by the app inside a canvas, naming the owner element by its stable id, so 0.4.0 adds it with no contract change; nothing in 0.3.0 produces it, as the served node id reserved the /// separator for virtual nodes.

The read changes nothing and runs no step, like snapshot, lint, graph, actions and a screenshot: it reads the engine's resolved layout and the computed style already turned into the layout style, with no second layout and no engine change.

Indirect, through the widening rule on the carriers: a new field of a closed value set (layout modes, placement kinds) or a number is not a widening; a new verb, an open value set, or a field carrying a page's style text (a length as authored, a property value) is the founder's fork and goes to the founder's forks list, not decided by the chunk.

The new read on every ratified carrier as lint, graph and actions were: the schema, the executor, the JSON forms, the command line, MCP's listing and results, the recording and replay of a kept check, and the self-description.
The capability statement and its pin name the new read; the statement's reach is edited by hand.

Indirect, through the driver's command span: it records the verb and, refused, the cause alone; no field holds the read's content or its size, under the log allowlist and redaction rules of escher's own targets.
The link to the lint: where a lint finding names an element and its bounds, this read is what tells its cause; whether the lint's answer points to it is P4's to settle.
Proven on the stand in both layout modes, with a minimal fixture beside it where the stand lacks a case: a flex child, a grid item, a positioned box, a scrolled or a transformed one.
A scrolled box's placement may read differently once Taffy moves past #1372 (reversed scroll origin); the chunk's checks of a scrolled case are the ones re-read at that take.

body_fields.convention: each new check is a Rust test over the session's own reads, not a browser or screen-reader harness
each stand expectation the new tests assert is stated once in a shared table, not restated per test
each new stand check runs repeated rounds in the slow-tier test leg and gates CI

body: Keyboard navigation and activation: Tab order, Enter and Space, range input keys, select list keys, the seven_guis grid and list keys; the read sends no input.
ARIA states and property reads and the role mapping: the read answers placement and size, not role, name or state.
The accessible name's precedence and labels naming their element.
Contrast thresholds, the contrast ratio formula, stand colours and scrollbar thumb strokes: the read measures no colour.
The open select list's colours, row heights, motion and its open state.
Password masking and value readings of form controls: the answer carries no control value.
Click and focus behaviour: a click focusing a control, disabled controls stopping a click, focus fixup and focus dropping on removal.
The Dioxus reached-handler record, handler coverage and UI graph state registration.
Cognitive accessibility: invalid state beyond colour or class.
Form event values and the input and change events a select fires.

**2026-11-15-taffy-from-upstream-git** (the three row entries and the take's ratification) — ~ decision/taffy-layout (Taffy 0.15 from upstream's git source pinned to one revision, part of blitz-dom's API through its signatures, no re-export), ~ decision/no-git-dependencies, ~ decision/deferred-upstream-dependency-bumps (Taffy from #1372 on, with its reversed-scroll-origin change, waits for its own take), and the eight git-Taffy layout commits at `e90751fd` ratified for that take alone. **2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces** (Taffy's tree traits on `LayoutPassState`; the bounds reader renamed; `writing-mode` opt-in) — + contract/layout/taffy-traits: the crate-private `LayoutPassState` implements Taffy's traversal and layout traits for one pass, and `BaseDocument` implements none. + contract/layout/stylo-taffy-exports: `to_taffy_style`, `TaffyStyloStyle`, `WritingMode`. Bounds go through `physical_unrounded_geometry`, which has two bodies, one with the `writing-mode` feature and one without. A read of the layout chain must work outside a layout pass, from `final_layout` and `to_taffy_style`, and must respect the writing-mode split.

**2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity** — + decision/normal-self-alignment-taffy: align/justify `normal` map to Taffy's NORMAL keyword, resolved by the aligned box's layout mode. decision/block-content-alignment-safe: the `safe` default reaches table cells. These alignment inputs are inputs the read reports «from the parent's alignment», and they are approximations the explanation must state as the engine applies them, not as CSS reads.

**2026-10-24-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** (the dropped-node hit skip, the replaced element's natural height and the recorded style facts) — ~ decision/node-holds-structure: `Node::out_of_flow`, written by the style traversal and read by `LayoutPassState::is_out_of_flow` alone, while `Node::is_out_of_flow` keeps its style reading. [Layout]: a replaced element's natural height follows its `aspect-ratio`. The read's «absolute or fixed positioning» kind and a replaced box's size come from these facts. Trap: the recorded flag and the style reading are two separate readers.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (the inline box's paint skip; the resolved `width`/`height`; a table box's layout damage; the key-press panic's fix; the orphan comment gone) — ~ decision/node-holds-structure gains the box-construction fact `IS_INLINE_WITH_ONLY_BLOCK_CHILDREN`. `resolved_style_value`'s width and height read `unrounded_layout()`, sub-pixel where `final_layout` rounds. + decision/anonymous-block-dealloc-detaches and decision/anonymous-block-drop-clears-layout-parent: a stale `layout_parent` no longer panics. The snapshot's `bounds` read `select_list_bounds` first, so an open list's row is placed by the engine's own overlay, not by Taffy. That is a placement kind the read must not misattribute.

The read's «any scroll or transform that moves it» clause must agree with these readers and their stated rotation limit.

**2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit** — + decision/client-rect-own-box and decision/client-rect-ignores-own-scroll: the shared bounds reader subtracts the scroll offsets of the containing-block chain above a node, never the node's own. These were ratified as a direct engine change for every document. **2026-10-18-engine-debts** (the geometry readers: the hit at `contain: paint`, `absolute_position`, the client rect under transforms; the PROVISIONAL batch ratified) — + decision/absolute-position-ancestor-scroll-only (guard `scrolled_box_absolute_position`). + decision/client-rect-under-transforms (guard `transformed_client_rect`): the border box is mapped through its own and every containing block's transform and read as an axis-aligned box. + decision/transformed-element-bounds and decision/hit-stops-at-paint-clip. The answer names the parent's layout mode as a closed word (block, flex, grid, inline, absolute or fixed positioning, a float) and the inputs that mode took from computed style: sizing, margins and offsets, the parent's alignment and gaps.
The answer names the containing block the element was placed in and any scroll offset or transform that moves it from where layout put it.

The placement kind is not a closed set: the shape reserves a kind for a box placed by the app inside a canvas, naming its owner element by stable id, so 0.4.0 adds it with no contract change; this mirrors the UI graph's reserved owner///key id form.

The read takes Taffy's resolved layout per node and the computed Stylo style already turned into the Taffy style; it runs no second layout, and an engine change, if one appears, is the founder's fork.

The widening rule decides the answer's fields: closed words (layout modes, placement kinds) and numbers inside an already ratified carrier are not a widening; a new verb, an open value set, or any field carrying a page's style text as the author wrote it is the founder's fork and goes to founder-forks.md while he is away.

If the read is a driver verb it is a new verb on every ratified carrier, as lint, graph and actions were: escher-session's command line commands and arguments, its answer line, the MCP role's tool listing and results, help, and the recording and replay of a kept check.
The new verb's refusals and exit statuses are read from the schema's exit-status table, and its session errors carry the session error object with its remedy, on stderr and as the MCP error ending.
The command span records the verb and, when refused, the cause alone; no span field holds the read's content or its size.
The read's output is read by an agent, not a person: one line on stdout in the command line role and one tool result in the MCP role, in the same written forms the other read verbs use.
The capability statement gains the new read and its pinned check is updated to the verb set the driver has.
The stable id the read takes is the same element id the snapshot, the UI graph line and the actions line use; an unknown or stale id is refused the way those verbs refuse it.
The link to lint: where a lint finding names an element, this read tells its cause; whether lint's answer points to it is left open.
Proven on the stand in both layout modes, with minimal fixtures for a case the stand lacks: a flex child, a grid item, a positioned box, a scrolled box, a transformed box.
Checks of a scrolled box's placement are marked to be re-read when Taffy moves past the scrollable-overflow change, which reverses the scroll origin for every document.
The bounds the read answers are in the logical viewport (physical size over total scale), the same coordinates the snapshot's bounds use.

body: The new placement read answers with an element's bounds (the same bounds the snapshot reads) and the chain that placed it: the parent's layout mode (block, flex, grid, inline, absolute or fixed positioning, float), the sizing, margins, offsets, alignment and gaps that mode took from the computed style, the containing block, and any scroll or transform. It changes nothing in the document, like snapshot, lint, graph and actions.

The answer's placement kind is not a closed set. It must be able to name an element placed by the app inside a canvas, with the owner given by its stable id, so 0.4.0 can add that case without a contract change. The UI graph reserved the owner-and-key id form the same way.

The read takes Taffy's final layout for each node and the computed Stylo style that was converted into the Taffy style. There is no second layout pass, and any engine change that turns out to be needed is the founder's fork.

If the read is a driver verb, it joins every ratified carrier: the schema, the executor, the written answer forms, the command line, MCP's tool listing and results, escher-session's stdout command answer and mcp JSON-RPC lines, the self-description help, and the hand-kept capability statement with its pin. This is ratified as a boundary widening, as lint, graph and actions were.

The driver's command span gets the new verb as its verb value and records cause only when the command is refused. No span field holds the read's content or its size, and the span's field count stays the same.
If the read is offered over MCP, its tool_call span carries the new tool name and one of the closed endings (accepted, refused, error), and the command span is its child.
Refusals of the read use the closed set of refusal cause names: not-found for an unknown stable id, malformed for bad arguments, and stale where the id no longer holds. It adds no free-text cause.

The widening rule sorts the answer's fields. Closed words (layout modes, placement kinds) and numbers inside an already ratified carrier are no widening. A new verb, or a field carrying a page's authored style text (a length as written, a property's value), is the founder's fork, which goes to founder-forks.md while he is away. P4 settles which of these the answer needs.

The read's answer is never logged and never echoed into telemetry, as with the graph answer and other answer-bearing types. The driver emits no event of its own and installs no subscriber, and session logs carry no page content: no geometry, no style values, no ids from the answer.

Recording and replay of a kept check of the new read: the recording file and kept check file hold its arguments, answer and answer digest. Committed kept checks hold no private data, and the recording stays within its bounds and its private directory.
The lint link: where a lint finding names an element, this read is what tells the finding's cause. P4 decides whether lint's answer points to it.
Proof on the stand in both layout modes, with minimal fixtures beside it for any case the stand lacks: a flex child, a grid item, a positioned box, and a scrolled or transformed box.
A check of a scrolled box's placement may read differently after the later Taffy take past #1372 (ScrollableOverflow, reversed scroll origin), so those checks are marked to be re-read at that take.
For a cold agent, the new read is a verb like graph and actions, and the counted verbs and verdict fields decide whether it is counted toward the agent's calls.

body: The new read itself: a read-only verb-like read that runs no step, moves no session state and changes nothing, as the actions, graph and lint reads do.

The element is named by its stable element id: the id is looked up anew on each call, an unknown, stale or detached one is refused as stale or not-found in the fixed refusal order, and no NodeId or other process-local handle crosses with the answer or is kept between calls.

The answer's content: bounds (as the snapshot already reads them), the parent's layout mode, the placement kind, the containing block, and scroll or transform offsets, as closed words and numbers; the answer holds no page content, no attribute text and no control value, and the value mask holds on every carrier it crosses.

The boundary widening rule over the answer: a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is no widening, while a new verb, a new carrier, an open value set, or a field carrying a page's style text as the author wrote it is the founder's fork, recorded and not decided while he is away.

The placement kind is not a closed set: the shape reserves placed by the app inside canvas X, naming the owner by its stable id, as the stable element id reserved its virtual-node form; that reservation is itself a value set question under the widening rule.

If the read is a driver verb: the closed driver verb schema and its single validation gate, one validation path for every carrier, the driver argument kinds (an id), and the new verb entering the driver verbs contract beside actions and graph as a boundary widening on every ratified carrier.

The command span for the read records its verb and, when refused, its cause alone; no span field holds the read's content or its size, one command span per call, and driver outcomes and screen content never reach a log.
Refusals of the read come from the closed refusal cause set, hold nothing a call supplied, are logged by cause name only, and no call-supplied input panics the driver or is echoed back.

The MCP crossing of the read: a fixed-text listing entry, a result inside the MCP result size bound, the MCP server never printing or panicking, and the committed capability statement of the MCP crossing with its pin kept true.

The command line and session socket crossing: the read's answer on the escher-session result line inside the driver command line answer bounds, the session socket replies carrying no attribute text and no NodeId.

The recording and replay of a kept check that holds the read: the kept check keeps each answer whole, as it holds the graph and actions answers, the recorded check file is read strictly as untrusted, and each replayed step runs through the session.

Read only from what the engine already holds — Taffy's final layout per node and the computed Stylo style mapped into Taffy's style — with no second layout; an engine change, should one appear, is the founder's fork under the engine-change rule.

Elements without a resolved layout or style: a never-styled or unstyled node answers none or is refused rather than read, as the snapshot and the text extent reader treat it, and a stale node id never panics.

Scroll and transform in the answer: the visible region read through transforms, a non-invertible transform, and programmatic scroll clamping bound how a moved box's offset is read; scrolled-case checks are re-read after Taffy moves past #1372, whose scroll origin change may alter them.
The answer's size: whether the read is paged or unpaged, as the graph and actions answers are unpaged, and the answer bounds every carrier enforces on it.
The lint's link: if P4 has a lint finding point to this read for its cause, the lint findings still hold no page content and still cross every ratified carrier as they do now.

The widening rule over the answer's fields: closed words (layout modes, placement kinds) and numbers are no widening; a field carrying the page's style text as the author wrote it, or a property's value, is the founder's fork, so the answer holds no such value unless it is ratified.
The command span for the new verb records the verb and, refused, the cause alone; no span or driver log line holds the answer's content or its size — fixed words and counts only.
Refusals of the new verb: a malformed, unknown, stale or not-found element id is refused by the fixed refusal causes in their order, with their remedy, changing nothing and echoing no input.
The answer travels the session wire and the snapshot-style byte budget: it stays inside the answer bound, and an oversize answer is refused as any other.

A scrolled or transformed box reads where it stands: the answer accounts for the scroll offset and transform; its checks of a scrolled case are re-read when Taffy moves past #1372 (reversed scroll origin).

The lint link: a lint finding that names an element (clipped, overlap, off-screen, zero-size, truncated) is what this reading explains the cause of; the lint findings and their order stay as they are unless the chunk's P4 joins them.

Proof on the seven_guis headless stand in both layout modes, on the bundled font with no skip, with minimal fixture pages stated in code beside it for a flex child, a grid item, a positioned box, and a scrolled or transformed one.

The new verb's command-line and MCP checks run the package's own binary over the socket session, unix-gated, each check owning its host; a recorded check of the new verb replays through the ordinary call path.
The new verb's unit and executor tests: table-driven tests over the layout modes count their rows, and a failing assertion prints no argument value.

each new check holds no sleep and no wall-clock read; time moves only by the virtual clock
each new unit test sits in an inline test module of its source file and is controlled red-before-green
each new fixture page or test datum is stated in code, the stand booting offline, nothing seeded
each new stand stand-in is hand-written, with no mocking library
each new stand check holds to the zero-failure budget across the repeated stand rounds

Virtual-clock, advance and timer-tick rows, and the settle and load-wait rows of acting verbs: the new verb reads and acts on nothing.

Upstream Dioxus bridge and buffered-render rows, and the blitz-tests manifest rows: the chunk takes nothing from upstream.
CI package-install, action-pinning, secrets, cache and artifact rows: the chunk changes no workflow.
